articles.title: Ian Rapoport shares encouraging update on Puka Nacua's calf injury
articles.summary: Ian Rapoport said that after Puka Nacua underwent testing on his injured calf, it's believed to be "more minor than anything else."
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was unable to finish practice on Thursday after suffering a calf injury, causing him to exit early. He's the latest Rams player to get hurt , joining a list that includes Davante Adams, Kobie Turner and Myles Garrett.

Fortunately, Nacua's injury isn't believed to be serious.

Ian Rapoport said on NFL Network Friday that Nacua underwent testing on his calf and it's believed to be "more minor than anything else." Rapoport stopped short of saying Nacua's removal from practice was "precautionary because it's not nothing," but Rapoport doesn't believe it's a "significant injury.

"Yesterday we learned that Puka Nacua left practice with a calf injury," he said. "Went to go have tests. My understanding is after the tests, it was more minor than anything else. I wouldn't say precautionary because it's not nothing, but at least not a significant injury. What that doesn't tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua will be able to play this weekend for the Los Angeles Rams. … I think it's safe to say Puka Nacua is up in the air for Sunday."

Nacua missed two games earlier this season with a hip/groin injury, which he also suffered in practice. It's unclear whether this calf injury will keep him out of Sunday's contest against the Las Vegas Raiders , especially considering how late in the week it occurred.

The Rams have one more practice on Friday before releasing their final injury report of the week. They will then have to make a final decision on his status 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday when inactives are due.

articles.title: Cairo Santos Lobbied Bears Coaches to Attempt Game-Sealing 58-Yard FG vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson's gutsy decision to let kicker Cairo Santos attempt a 58-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots was heavily influenced by Santos himself.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson's gutsy decision to let kicker Cairo Santos attempt a 58-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots was heavily influenced by Santos himself.

Santos told reporters after the game that he was vocal about wanting the opportunity to try the kick, saying, "I was talking to [special teams coordinator Richard Hightower] HT that I felt good about the line. And then Ben asked, 'Does he want it?' And I heard it and I told HT, 'I want it.' And then Ben said he wants it. I'm thankful that Ben trusts me on that."

NFL legend announces Parkinson's diagnosis

Johnson confirmed the pre-kick conversation, saying, "One, we felt good about being inside that line, and two, we asked him, he said, 'Absolutely, I need redemption because I missed one earlier.' He came through for us in a big way."

Santos missed a 53-yard field goal earlier in the fourth quarter, so when Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was sacked, pushing Chicago to the edge of field goal range, it seemed likely that Johnson would punt the ball back to New England.

Instead, Johnson put his trust in Santos, who nailed a new career long to extend the Chicago lead to nine with 1:34 remaining in the fourth quarter, essentially putting the game away.

After a Patriots field goal, the Bears recovered an onside kick, and clinched a 5-2 start to the season in the process.

articles.title: Colts QB Anthony Richardson Sr. reportedly charged with marijuana possession
articles.summary: A bench trial has been scheduled for Jan. 4, 2027.
articles.body:
Anthony Richardson Sr. of the Indianapolis Colts is facing a misdemeanor charge for possession of marijuana following an Oct. 12 traffic stop in Carmel, Indiana, according to FOX59 .

"We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information," the Colts said in a statement. "We will have no further comment at this time."

Court documents obtained by FOX59/CBS4 show that charges were filed on Monday, a week after police officers stopped Richardson's black 2023 Dodge Charger. The vehicle's registration was reportedly expired and was assigned to a different car.

According to police, the car pulled over to the side of the road and officers noticed the "odor of marijuana" as they approached.

Richardson reportedly admitted that he did smoke marijuana in the car so as to not do so in front of his children. He also told police that he possessed a small amount of marijuana in the car.

The quarterback was handcuffed after exiting the car and officers proceeded with searching the vehicle. A small mason jar was reportedly found containing a substance believed to be marijuana and a bag of THC-infused gummies that was opened.

The substance reportedly tested positive for THC. Richardson was not arrested, released and was cited for the expired registration and received a summons for possession of marijuana.

A hearing was scheduled for Dec. 9, but has since been waived. A bench trial will be held on Jan. 2027.

Richardson is the second Colts player to have a run-in with police this season. Wide receiver Keenan Allen was charged with two misdemeanors following his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker's Seahawks Split Detailed in New NFL Rumors Ahead of Revenge Game with Chiefs
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks' willingness to let Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III walk in free agency was tied to doubts regarding his injury history, ESPN's Nate Taylor and Brady Henderson reported Friday.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks' willingness to let Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III walk in free agency was tied to doubts regarding his injury history, ESPN's Nate Taylor and Brady Henderson reported Friday.

According to Taylor and Henderson, Seahawks "decision-makers had reservations about [Walker's] availability dating to his rookie season."

Because of those reservations, the Seahawks were "only willing to go as high as roughly $10 million per season to re-sign him in March," Taylor and Henderson reported.

The Athletic's Michael-Shawn Dugar had previously reported the Seahawks never held "serious discussions" about re-signing Walker, and did not offer the running back a contract ahead of free agency.

Walker ultimately joined the Kansas City Chiefs on a three-year, $43.05 million contract featuring $28.7 million in guaranteed money.

That wasn't the first time the Seahawks had hesitated to commit to Walker going forward. Taylor and Henderson reported concerns regarding Walker's early-career injuries also contributed to the Seahawks drafting Zach Charbonnet in 2023 and a backfield split between Charbonnet and Walker last season.

After he was selected by the Seahawks in the second round of the 2022 draft, Walker missed multiple games in each of his first three NFL campaigns with injuries including a sports hernia as well as shoulder, ankle, oblique and calf issues.

He did not miss more than two games in a row over that span, although he sat out four of the last five games of the Seahawks' 2024 season.

Walker then appeared in all 17 games of a 2025 season during which he played a career-low 47 percent of Seattle's offensive snaps as Charbonnet took over some of his workload.

That has flipped in Kansas City despite Walker missing time during the preseason with foot and ankle issues . The running back has taken a career-high 75 percent of snaps through five games while racking up an NFL-high 665 rushing yards on 106 carries.

The Seahawks, on the other hand, have been unable to replace Walker's production with Charbonnet on the PUP list to start the season amid his recovery from a torn ACL. Seattle ranks 18th in the NFL in total rushing yards through Week 6.

Charbonnet has been activated and could make his season debut against the Chiefs, while Walker will look to prove to his former team he can thrive with a full workload when the Week 7 matchup kicks off Sunday at Lumen Field.

articles.title: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer Calls Himself 'Elite Play-Caller' amid Offense's Struggles
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has maintained a high opinion of his own play-calling despite his team's 2-4 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has maintained a high opinion of his own play-calling despite his team's 2-4 start to the 2026 season.

"I have incredible confidence in our offense. Have not played well the last two weeks. We understand a lot of the reasons why, have addressed a lot of the reasons why," Schottenheimer said in a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

"We haven't changed who we are," Schottenheimer added. "We're still a good explosive offense with weapons. We can hurt you a lot of different ways. Certainly have not lost the ability to call plays.

Schottenheimer 'Pissed Off' by Cowboys Start

"I'm an elite play-caller in this league, and I think that that can turn around quickly."

Schottenheimer was also asked if he had given any consideration to turning over play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Klayton Adams.

"No. Absolutely not," Schottenheimer responded.

The Cowboys are preparing to take on the Philadelphia Eagles Monday night at Lincoln Financial Field.

Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones said on his own appearance on 105.3 The Fan earlier this week that he and owner Jerry Jones felt "really good about our coaching staff."

"There's not any question in Jerry's or my mind. He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen," Jones said.

Schottenheimer has previously been critical this season of his own play-calling, which he gave an "F" grade after a Week 3 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.

The Cowboys are now heading into Week 7, having been held to fewer than 17 points twice in consecutive losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers.

Dallas began last Sunday's matchup against the Packers with a six-play, 19-yard drive before punting the ball away and going on to trail for the remainder of the loss.

Schottenheimer, who said in his introductory press conference back in 2025 he was a "big believer in shifts and motions to distort things," has moved away from that tactic in his second season as head coach. The Cowboys rank second to last in the NFL with a 42.7 percent motion rate so far this season, per Sharp Football.

Adams called plays in one of the Cowboys' preseason matchups, while offensive pass game specialist Ken Dorsey boasts previous play calling experience .

Whether Schottenheimer is able to run a more flexible offense next week against the Eagles could determine whether the Cowboys ultimately considers either staffer as play-calling options down the stretch.

articles.title: La NFL se topa de bruces con el caos de las protestas de París
articles.standfirst: El fútbol americano llega por primera vez a Francia y lo hace en medio de las protestas. Los Steelers han optado por cancelar su evento con aficionados
articles.summary: El fútbol americano llega por primera vez a Francia y lo hace en medio de las protestas. Los Steelers han optado por cancelar su evento con aficionados
articles.body: Este sábado París se prepara para nuevas protestas y, a tenor de cómo fueron las cosas la semana pasada, se van a intensificar las medidas de seguridad. Este sábado en la capital francesa se desplegarán 70.000 policías y gendarmes para evitar nuevos desórdenes durante las protestas sociales previstas. Recordemos que en la convocatoria de hace casi una semana se detuvo a más de 2.000 personas por su participación en actos de violencia. En este clima aterriza por primera vez la NFL en Francia, en concreto en la ciudad de París, donde New Orleans Saints y los Pittsburgh Steelers se enfrentarán el domingo. El comisionado de la NFL Roger Goodell ha reiterado estos últimos días que todo estará bajo control para que el partido se pueda celebrar sin problemas, pero ya ayer los Steelers cancelaron uno de sus eventos del fin de semana previstos para aficionados. "Tras los recientes acontecimientos en el barrio de la Bastilla y después de una cuidadosa consideración, creemos oportuno no seguir adelante con el evento para aficionados Steelers House previsto en París", anunció el club. Se trata del primer escollo de un fin de semana que tenía que servir de promoción para NFL y que se va a ver empañado por el clima de violencia que vive la ciudad. A principios de esta semana, Dani Watt, esposa del ala defensiva de los Steelers, TJ Watt, cuestionó públicamente por qué no se ha cambiado la fecha del partido. En cualquier caso, la NFL comunicó ayer que su evento denominado NFL Fan House, programado para el viernes y el sábado, se mantiene según lo previsto. El propio Goodell, tras salir de la reunión de otoño de propietarios, confirmó que asistirá al partido y dijo que en los últimos días había hablado con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, sobre el evento y la posibilidad de seguir adelante con el partido. El comisionado se mostró confiado y trató de tranquilizar con sus palabras: "Hemos hecho todos los preparativos necesarios. Nos hemos puesto en contacto con todas las autoridades pertinentes". El partido entre Saints y Steelers tiene lugar en el Stade de France, el recinto de la vergonzosa final de Champions League de 2022 entre el Real Madrid y el Liverpool donde la seguridad brilló por su ausencia y la organización fue un caos indescriptible. Esperemos que el amplio perímetro de seguridad que se organiza en torno a los recintos donde se disputan los partidos de la NFL en el extranjero surta efecto, pues aquel 30 de mayo de 2022 un ejército de delincuentes organizados atormentó a los aficionados de ambos equipos que se desplazaron al estadio.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s minority ownership stake in the Las Vegas Aces draws attention as team valuation climbs from $310 million in 2025 to $420 million in 2026
articles.summary: Tom Brady built his name by winning Super Bowls, but his ambitions now reach well beyond the football field.
articles.body: Tom Brady built his name by winning Super Bowls, but his ambitions now reach well beyond the football field. The seven-time champion has stepped into the business of professional sports ownership, including a minority stake in the Las Vegas Aces. The WNBA franchise has seen its estimated value rise from $310 million in 2025 to $420 million in 2026, putting the growth of women's basketball in the spotlight. The increase highlights the commercial potential of the league, while raising a bigger question: how much could rising team values mean for investors such as Brady?Tom Brady’s minority ownership in the Las Vegas AcesBrady's connection to the Las Vegas Aces adds a new dimension to his career after football. Rather than focusing only on his broadcasting work and other business interests, he has also entered the ownership side of professional sports. His role as a minority owner gives him a stake in the franchise without placing him in control of its day-to-day operations.Minority ownership can offer a way to benefit from a team's long-term growth. If a franchise becomes more valuable, the value of an investor's stake may rise as well. However, the financial result depends on the size of the holding, the terms of the investment, the team's financial performance and any future sale.Brady's exact ownership percentage and the price he paid for his stake have not been publicly established in the figures discussed here. That means it would be misleading to calculate his personal gains using the team's full valuation alone.His involvement still carries significance. Brady is one of the most recognisable figures in American sports, and his move into ownership reflects a wider trend of athletes investing in teams and businesses after building their careers on the field. His profile may also help draw more attention to the Aces and the WNBA, although celebrity involvement alone does not guarantee financial success.Las Vegas Aces valuation rises from $310 million in 2025 to $420 million in 2026The Aces' reported valuation climbed by $110 million in a year. Forbes valued the Aces at $310 million in 2025 and $420 million in 2026, a 35% increase. That represents an increase of roughly 35.5%, a notable jump for a franchise competing in a rapidly changing sports market.The figures point to the growing financial interest surrounding women's basketball. Team values can reflect several factors, including ticket sales, sponsorship agreements, media income, merchandise, fan engagement and expectations about future revenue. Investors may also consider the strength of a team's brand and its ability to attract audiences beyond its home market.A valuation is not the same as annual revenue or cash profit. It is an estimate of what a business could be worth under certain market conditions. A franchise may command a higher valuation because investors expect future growth, even if its current income does not rise at the same pace.That distinction matters when looking at the Aces' $420 million valuation. The increase suggests that the market sees greater potential in the franchise, but it does not mean the team has generated an extra $110 million in cash or that every owner has received a payout.For Brady, the rise provides a reason to watch the investment closely. If the Aces continue to build their commercial reach and their estimated value increases, minority shareholders could benefit. Still, any actual return would depend on the terms of their investments and whether they eventually sell their shares or receive distributions.Why the WNBA’s growth matters for sports investorsThe Aces' rising value also reflects a wider shift in how investors view women's professional sports. For years, women's leagues often received less media coverage and commercial attention than men's competitions. That gap remains a challenge, but growing audiences and stronger business interest have made women's basketball a more prominent investment opportunity.The WNBA's appeal rests on more than the results of individual games. Its teams can build loyal local fan bases, develop recognisable players and create connections with younger audiences. Sponsorships, live events and digital platforms can help turn that interest into lasting commercial relationships.For investors, the key question is whether growing attention can translate into reliable income over time. Higher attendance and stronger sponsorship demand can support a team's finances, while media agreements may influence the value of the league as a whole. Better facilities, marketing and fan experiences can also help teams deepen their connection with supporters.However, growth is not automatic. Teams still face operating costs, competition for audiences and the challenge of turning popularity into sustainable earnings. A higher valuation may reflect optimism about future performance, but that optimism must eventually be supported by results.The Aces are therefore part of a bigger story about the business of women's sports. Their valuation offers one measure of investor confidence, though it cannot by itself explain every factor behind the increase. The long-term test will be whether the league can continue to expand its audience and build revenue streams that support its teams.Could the Las Vegas Aces’ rising value boost Tom Brady’s investment?The rise from $310 million to $420 million gives Brady's minority ownership a clear financial angle, but it does not reveal the exact value of his personal holding. To estimate that, readers would need to know his ownership percentage, the investment's original terms and whether the reported valuation applies directly to the stake.For example, an investor who owns a small share of a franchise may see the estimated value of that holding rise when the overall business becomes more valuable. But the increase remains an unrealised gain unless the investor sells the stake or receives money through another arrangement. The final amount can also depend on debt, ownership agreements and the terms of any transaction.Brady's wider sports profile may make his investment choices especially interesting to fans. His career has already given him experience in a high-value professional league, while his work beyond football has broadened his business interests. Team ownership offers a different challenge: the focus shifts from performance on the field to long-term financial planning, brand development and the changing economics of sports.For now, the Aces' valuation growth is best understood as a sign of the franchise's rising estimated market value, not proof of a specific profit for Brady. The next stage will depend on the team's business performance and the wider direction of the WNBA.The numbers are striking: $310 million in 2025 and $420 million in 2026. Whether that growth continues will matter to the Aces, their investors and anyone watching the expanding business of women's basketball.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cole Kmet Has 'Serious' Knee Injury, Latest Rumors on Timeline to Return to Bears
articles.summary: Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet is believed to have suffered a season-ending knee injury in Thursday's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet is believed to have suffered a season-ending knee injury in Thursday's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Kmet suffered a "serious" injury that will end his season.

Biggest takeaways from Bears' win over Patriots

The injury occurred late in the fourth quarter when Kmet caught a pass near the sideline, turned up field and was tackled by Christian Gonzalez and Robert Spillane.

Kmet immediately grabbed at his knee after hitting the ground. He was taken off the field on a cart.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson didn't have an official update on Kmet's status when asked after the game, though he noted it seemed bad.

"We'll know more about it tomorrow, but I don't think it looked very good," Johnson said .

Kmet finished the game with 28 yards on three receptions. He appeared in each of Chicago's first seven games this season, recording 87 yards and one touchdown on 10 catches.

A seven-year veteran, Kmet has spent his entire NFL career with the Bears. The 27-year-old ranks second among all tight ends in franchise history in receiving yards, receptions and receiving touchdowns.

The Bears still have Colston Loveland as their No. 1 tight end, but Johnson has liked using multiple tight-end formations that get Kmet on the field. He played at least 55 percent of the offensive snaps in six of the first seven games this season.

If Kmet is out for an extended period of time, Sam Roush will likely step into the role as the No. 2 tight end. Roush is a rookie third-round draft pick who has played 114 snaps so far this season.

The Bears have won two straight games and moved into sole possession of second place in the NFC North with their victory over New England.

articles.title: Why did Colts QB Anthony Richardson tell police he smoked marijuana in his car before misdemeanor charge
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. is facing a misdemeanor marijuana possession charge after an Oct. 12 traffic stop in Carmel, Ind.
articles.body: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. is facing a misdemeanor marijuana possession charge after an Oct. 12 traffic stop in Carmel, Ind. Police reportedly found marijuana and THC-infused gummies inside his vehicle, according to court documents.But Richardson's explanation to officers has drawn attention. The 24-year-old reportedly admitted to smoking marijuana inside his car because he wanted to avoid doing so around his children at home. He was allowed to leave without being arrested, although the encounter resulted in a criminal charge filed on Oct. 19.What did Anthony Richardson Sr. tell police during the marijuana possession incident?Richardson was driving a black 2023 Dodge Charger when a Carmel police officer stopped him on Oct. 12. According to NFL insider Ari Meirov and FOX59/CBS4, which first reported the case, the vehicle's registration had expired and was assigned to another car.The officer reported smelling marijuana while approaching Richardson's vehicle. When questioned about the smell, Richardson allegedly acknowledged smoking marijuana inside the car and possessing a small amount.According to court documents cited by ESPN's Stephen Holder, Richardson explained that he had smoked inside the vehicle because he did not want to smoke marijuana at home around his children.Officers then instructed Richardson to step outside and detained him in handcuffs while searching the vehicle.The search reportedly uncovered a small mason jar containing suspected marijuana and an opened package of THC-infused gummies. ESPN reported that the gummies contained 500 milligrams of THC.According to FOX59/CBS4, subsequent testing returned positive results for THC. Police confiscated the substances.Richardson was not arrested or taken to jail. Officers issued a citation for the expired registration and a summons for marijuana possession before allowing him to leave.The Hamilton County prosecutor's office filed the misdemeanor charge on Monday, Oct. 19, one week after the traffic stop.The distinction matters. Although Richardson was temporarily handcuffed during the search, the reports indicate that officers released him at the scene.The Colts addressed the situation Friday after the charge became public."We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information," the team said in a statement reported by ESPN. "We will have no further comment at this time."Richardson has been charged, but he has not been convicted. The allegations will be addressed through the court process.What happens next for Anthony Richardson Sr. as his Colts contract approaches its end?Richardson's legal case has a scheduled court date. His future with Indianapolis, however, was already uncertain before the charge became public.According to FOX59/CBS4, Richardson's initial hearing, previously scheduled for Dec. 9, has been waived. Court records list a bench trial for Jan. 4, 2027.A bench trial means a judge, rather than a jury, will determine the outcome. The scheduled date could change as the proceedings continue.There has been no confirmed announcement of disciplinary action from the Colts or the NFL related to the misdemeanor charge.For Richardson, the timing comes during a season in which he has yet to appear in a regular-season game.Indianapolis selected the former Florida quarterback with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. At the time, his combination of arm strength and rushing ability made him one of the draft's most closely watched quarterback prospects.However, his first three NFL seasons did not establish him as Indianapolis' long-term starter.Richardson recorded an 8-7 record as a starter across the 2023 and 2024 seasons. His career passing totals include 2,400 yards, 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions, along with 10 rushing touchdowns.He subsequently lost the starting job to Daniel Jones, who remains ahead of him on the Colts' depth chart.Richardson sought a trade earlier in 2026 but remained with Indianapolis. The organization also declined his fifth-year contract option in April, leaving him in the final season of his rookie deal.That decision means Richardson is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 season unless his contract situation changes.The misdemeanor case does not automatically mean Indianapolis will release him or that the NFL will suspend him. Neither outcome has been announced.Nevertheless, Richardson faces two separate questions about his future: how the legal proceedings will conclude and whether he can earn another opportunity to start in the NFL.The Colts are preparing to face the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Oct. 25, with Jones expected to start at quarterback.Richardson's next scheduled legal proceeding is the Jan. 4 bench trial. His playing future remains unresolved as the final year of his Colts contract continues.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Eligible to Play vs. Ravens After NFL Reduces Discipline Upon Appeal
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills linebacker Sam Franklin Jr. will be eligible to play in Week 8 when the team returns from a bye after having his discipline reduced.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills linebacker Sam Franklin Jr. will be eligible to play in Week 8 when the team returns from a bye after having his discipline reduced.

Michael Signora, NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, announced on Friday that Franklin's appeal of his one-game suspension was reduced to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct by hearing officer James Thrash.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that Franklin was being suspended for one game due to "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" during Buffalo's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6.

Franklin was said to have spit on a Raiders player during an extra-point attempt late in the fourth quarter.

In a post on Instagram after the league announced its discipline, Franklin denied any wrongdoing: "Not a dirty player what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone!"

"As we said from the start, Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did," Franklin's agents said in a statement . "We're glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review.

"It's unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely. We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player's conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game. We're glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday."

Franklin was one of two Bills players disciplined for their actions during the Raiders game. C.J. Gardner-Johnson was suspended one game for spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.

Officials flagged Gardner-Johnson for unsportsmanlike conduct and he was ejected from the game as a result of the incident. He issued an apology on social media following the Bills' win.

The Bills are on bye this week and will return to action on Nov. 1 in a marquee matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo has won back-to-back games after suffering its first loss of the season against the New England Patriots in Week 4.

Franklin is in his second season with the Bills after originally joining their practice squad in August 2025. He has appeared in 23 consecutive games since the start of last season.

The 30-year-old Franklin has six combined tackles in six games in 2026.

articles.title: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Timeline to Return to Practice After Surgery
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams star defender Myles Garrett could potentially be available to rejoin the active roster as soon as Week 8.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star defender Myles Garrett could potentially be available to rejoin the active roster as soon as Week 8.

ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Friday on the Pat McAfee Show it is "likely" Garrett returns to practice next week.

Garrett, who underwent knee surgery ahead of Week 2, has already been ruled out for a Week 7 game at the Las Vegas Raiders.

Returning to practice will mark the opening of a 21-day window during which the Rams can activate Garrett from IR.

Garrett has been sidelined since Week 1 after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his knee in September.

Should Garrett return to practice next Wednesday, that window could encompass games against the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals before the Rams break for their Week 11 bye.

Garrett played 46 snaps in his Rams debut before undergoing surgery on an injury Rapoport reported had impacted him since training camp.

The star defender said he had been limited by the injury when he was held without a tackle in a Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Rapoport reported in September Garrett had been given an expected recovery timeline of six weeks.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones later reported one Rams source saw that six-week timeline as a "worst-case scenario," and that a second source predicted Garrett would be available for Week 7.

Garrett will now be out at least until Week 8, and reporters differ in their optimism as to when he will return. ESPN's Dan Graziano estimated earlier this week Garrett would be "likely out for another two or three weeks at least."

The Rams have gone 2-3 in five games without Garrett while failing to live up to last year's status as the most productive offense in football.

articles.title: Steelers face another setback in France as team forced to cancel second event, this time because of weather
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers canceled practice and a Paris fan event ahead of their historic NFL game against the New Orleans Saints at Stade de France.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers are canceling events left in right in France even as plans for Sunday's regular-season game against the New Orleans Saints remains on track. The Steelers arrived in the country on Friday morning after a Thursday evening flight from Western Pennsylvania. The plan was for the team to go from the airport to a practice, but that never happened. Practice was instead canceled. STEELERS CANCEL PARIS FAN EVENT OVER FEARS OF UNREST WHILE NFL PUSHES AHEAD WITH ITS OWN EVENT And, no, it wasn't because of the civil unrest that has been in the news for a couple of weeks. It was that darn French wind. "We had two plans coming in," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Friday. "Just really wanted to activate the players after the long flight, just based off the communication with the weather, and just in reality of the timing too. "We had to make the decision before we landed just to put it together. So, but frankly, driving by it, I wish we would have stopped. But this is part of our plan, so we thought it'd be definitely activating." NFL FRANCE PREPARATIONS CONTINUE AS STEELERS SPEAK WITH LEAGUE, LOUISIANA GOV JEFF LANDRY HEADS TO PARIS Winds in the area were reported at a steady 20 mph so one might understand the team's decision not to trek over to practice. And no civil unrest has been reported in the area regardless of that being a problem in past days. It's a problem McCarthy says is on his mind. "Oh, definitely," he said. "It's my responsibility to always be aware of anything that surrounds our football team, so definitely in tune. I think the NFL, the local government and everybody involved have done an excellent job communicating. "We're very confident in our experience here is going to be very positive." The Steelers on Thursday canceled their Fan House event for fans in Paris because of the events of past days. The team released a statement to OutKick about that cancellation. "We are honored to play in the first-ever regular season NFL game in France. "The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites. "As a precautionary measure, the Steelers designated bar that had been planned in Bastille – an area that has experienced recent disruptions – will not proceed. EXCLUSIVE: SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO GIVES NFL COMMISSIONER ASSURANCES THAT GAME IN FRANCE 'WILL BE FINE' "We continue to look forward to the game versus the Saints this Sunday at the Stade de France." The Saints have so far experienced no operational setbacks that have been reported. And the Steelers hope they can also get on track and on schedule after Friday. "We just arrived, so we're right on schedule so far," McCarthy said with a laugh. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: NFL Paris 2026: Aaron Rodgers and his magnificent obsession ready for more NFL history in final season of storied career
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers tells Sky Sports he is on the '18th green' of his NFL career amid what marks his final season; watch Rodgers' Steelers take on the New Orleans Saints at Stade de France in Paris, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1pm Sunday
articles.body:
It is the game he cannot say goodbye to, but one he will say goodbye to at the end of this season, which he has insisted shall be the last of his stellar Hall of Fame career.

Just moments earlier Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy had been asked about the difference in the Rodgers of now compared to the Rodgers with whom he had worked and won a Super Bowl in Green Bay. More grey hairs was the first answer.

But at the age of 42 Rodgers will lead the Steelers out as a prized attraction when they face the New Orleans Saints in the NFL's historic Paris debut at Stade de France on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

"To steal a line from one of my all-time favourite movies, 'Obsession is a young man's game'," Rodgers told Sky Sports.

"And the NFL is the young man's game. I'm hanging on and enjoying this last one."

So often the four-time MVP has likened his latter years to being on the proverbial 'back nine' of his NFL career, continuing to ride the highs and lows of a game that hasn't always fallen in his favour.

"I think I'm on the 18th green!" he laughed."

Rodgers has thrown for a ninth-most 1,487 yards and 12 touchdowns to five interceptions across Pittsburgh's 4-2 start to the season, having been reunited with former Packers coach McCarthy following Mike Tomlin's exit. His quest to win an elusive second Super Bowl ring may not have materialised as planned, but he is at peace with what awaits at the end of his 22nd campaign.

"I've given a lot to this game, the game has given me a lot in return. I've got zero qualms about this being the end, zero fears about what's next. I'm just trying to live in the moment and enjoy this time with these guys."

Rodgers has long embraced opportunities to reach different corners of the world through football, last year being a leading advocate for Pittsburgh's historic appearance in Dublin and now preparing to be part of another milestone for the NFL in France.

"There's definitely only one moment in France," he said. "I'm going to enjoy this for the next couple of days. It's fun to be out here.

"It's fun to be a part of the first. As you get older you don't get a lot of firsts. To be in the first game in Paris is special.

"That's part of the game; that's the beauty of the game. It's going to keep on rolling. You're going to be here for a short time. You've got to enjoy it. Because you never know when it's going to be done. We've all been blessed.

"I'm just thankful for the game and the places it's taken me. We've been to a lot of different countries now to play games."

It is a welcome return to these shores for Rodgers, who recalled the time he was mobbed by Packers fans after entering the WOS Bar during a previous trip to Paris.

He and the Steelers landed in the French capital on just Friday morning following a red-eye flight from Pittsburgh, while the Saints came into town on Monday as the designated home team.

"I've played in three countries now, and each of them we've left on Thursday early evening. Would have been nice one time to come over on a Monday," he said.

articles.title: Traffic Stop Leads to Misdemeanor Marijuana Possession Charge Against Colts QB Anthony Richardson
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts backup quarterback Anthony Richardson faces a misdemeanor possession of marijuana charge following a traffic stop earlier this month. The charge was filed Monday.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts backup quarterback Anthony Richardson faces a misdemeanor possession of marijuana charge following a traffic stop earlier this month. The charge was filed Monday.

The affidavit from the Hamilton County prosecutor's office said a police officer stopped Richardson on Oct. 12 because the car he was driving had an expired registration tag. The license plate on the car also did not match the one listed on the registration.

The officer wrote that when he approached the vehicle, he smelled marijuana.

According to the affidavit, Richardson acknowledged he had been smoking marijuana inside the car because he did not want to smoke it around his children. The officer wrote that Richardson said he had a small amount of marijuana in the car. The officer said he found a "leafy, green material" he believed to be marijuana along with a bag of five marijuana gummies inside a small Mason jar in the car's glove compartment.

Richardson's attorney, James Voyles, declined to comment on the case.

"We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information," the Colts said in a statement. "We will have no further comment at this time."

Richardson has not played in a game since Oct. 5, 2025.

The Colts (2-4) selected the former Florida Gators star with the No. 4 overall draft pick in 2023. But after winning the starting job during his first training camp, he has been plagued by injuries and inconsistency.

Richardson appeared in just four games in 2023 before suffering a season-ending shoulder injury. He started a career-high 11 games in 2024 but completed just 47.7% of his passes, the lowest among all NFL starters that season, and threw eight touchdown passes and 12 interceptions. He also took himself out of a game that season, later acknowledging he was "tired."

In 2025, Daniel Jones beat out Richardson for the starting job in training camp. Richardson wound up throwing just two total passes in two games before suffering a fractured orbital bone near his right eye when a stretching band broke in the locker room before a game. He hasn't played a snap since and has made two requests to be traded.

This summer Richardson beat out Riley Leonard for the No. 2 job in training camp. But Jones has taken every snap this season since returning from a torn right Achilles tendon he suffered last December.

Earlier this week, the Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard — who was running the team when Richardson was drafted. On Wednesday, Richardson said he was disappointed with the change and that he wanted to prove Ballard was right in drafting him.

"He believed in me enough to have me here, and I'm forever grateful for that," Richardson said. "I'm trying to do my part and not make him feel like he made the wrong decision. So I'm just trying to keep getting better every week and am waiting on my opportunity."

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Reacts to Najee Harris Being Released by John Harbaugh's Giants, 'Nobody Is Safe'
articles.summary: Running back Cam Skattebo feels the New York Giants were sending a message to players by releasing Najee Harris ahead of Week 7.
articles.body:
Running back Cam Skattebo feels the New York Giants were sending a message to players by releasing Najee Harris ahead of Week 7.

"Nobody is safe, that's as simple as that," Skattebo told reporters Friday (h/t ESPN's Jordan Raanan). "When we go on the field, and we go perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here."

Skattebo concluded, "If I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here."

Harris was cut just two days after starting for the Giants in a Week 6 loss to the visiting New Orleans Saints.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Friday the decision to release Harris was made because "it's hard to carry four backs."

"There were some other moves we had to make to get guys on the roster... Like I told him, nothing against what he did. I thought he ran super hard," Harbaugh said.

Harris recorded nine carries for just 11 yards while adding one catch for five yards in his final two games with the Giants. He expressed frustration after the game with the Giants' lack of consistent use of their running backs.

"It's hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays...if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do," Harris said Sunday, per SNY .

Harris most recently recorded four touches against the Saints as Skattebo was held without a carry in the loss. Skattebo said Friday he felt he had been "taught a lesson" by the zero-carry outing.

Harbaugh indicated he was expecting a bigger role for Skattebo now that the Giants' running back depth chart features only him, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary.

"He always going to be a big part of our season, and he had a heck of a week of practice," Harbaugh said about Skattebo.

The Giants announced Wednesday quarterback J.J. McCarthy would be starting in place of Jameis Winston after replacing him late in the loss to the Saints.

Harbaugh will hope a quarterback switch and a less varied workload for his running backs will help the Giants (3-2-1) hold on to their NFC East lead with a win over the Houston Texans (2-4). Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Houston.

articles.title: Atlanta Falcons' Social Media Post of Their Throwback Logo Causes a Stir Online
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — A social media post by the NFL's Atlanta Falcons of their throwback logo on a red, white, gold and black striped background has caused a stir online, with replies noting its resemblance to symbols from Nazi Germany.
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — A social media post by the NFL's Atlanta Falcons of their throwback logo on a red, white, gold and black striped background has caused a stir online, with replies noting its resemblance to symbols from Nazi Germany.

The logo release provoked thousands of responses on social media, many of them memes that mocked the design.

The logo coincides with the Falcons wearing throwback uniforms Sunday at home against unbeaten San Francisco. That includes the team's primary logo from 1989-2002 of a right-facing black and white falcon. The widely panned background is not part of the throwback helmets or uniforms.

A message sent to the Falcons seeking comment Friday was not immediately returned. An NFL spokesperson did not immediately respond to a message asking for comment.

Team owner Arthur Blank is Jewish and has donated significant money and offered support for Holocaust remembrance causes, through the Molly Blank Fund in the name of his mother. That included $1.5 million to the US Holocaust Memorial Museum in 2023.

articles.title: NFL reduces punishment Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. received for allegedly spitting, changes 1-game suspension to fine
articles.summary: Franklin reportedly denied the incident ever happened in Buffalo's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
One of the two Buffalo Bills defensive backs who were handed one-game suspensions by the NFL for spitting during last week's win over the Las Vegas Raiders will no longer be prohibited from playing in the Bills' next game.

Whereas C.J. Gardner-Johnson will still be out for a Nov. 1 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens , fellow Buffalo safety Sam Franklin Jr. — a special teams captain — saw his punishment for allegedly spitting on a Raiders player reduced on Friday from a single-game ban to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct.

The change was made by hearing officer James Thrash , who was jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFL Players Association.

On Wednesday, when the league announced Franklin's suspension , Franklin denied the alleged incident ever happened and wound up appealing.

In the NFL's release revealing Franklin's suspension earlier this week, the league pointed to the aftermath of a Raiders extra point with less than two minutes left in the game.

That Wednesday memo from the league read: "With 1:32 remaining in the fourth quarter following Las Vegas' successful extra-point attempt, Franklin Jr. spit at an opponent, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.'"

According to a Wednesday report from ESPN , Franklin posted a slow-motion replay of that PAT to his Instagram stories hours after the suspension was announced. He reportedly supplied the caption, "Not a dirty play what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone."

At the bottom of the clip, per ESPN, Franklin added the hashtag "#notthemcnuggets," indicating that he took a shot below the belt on the play.

Notably, Franklin wasn't penalized in the moment, unlike Gardner-Johnson, who was flagged and ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct after he spit toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers late in the first half.

In a statement Friday, Franklin's agents, Harold C. Lewis and Christian Addison, said, "Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did," via NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix .

The statement continued: "We're glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review. It's unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely. We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player's conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game. We're glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday."

Because the Bills are on bye this week, Franklin's suspension wasn't supposed to begin until next Monday. He would have had to sit out the team's Week 8 contest versus the Ravens.

Since Franklin won his appeal, though, the special teamer be available for that matchup. The Temple product is now in his second season with Buffalo and his seventh NFL campaign overall. So far this time around, he's piled up 132 special teams snaps, per Pro Football Focus. Along the way, he's tallied six total tackles.

As for Gardner-Johnson, his suspension was upheld Thursday.

articles.title: Patriots Rookie TreVeyon Henderson Struggles in Unexpected Area
articles.summary: The Patriots drafted Henderson with confidence in his pass protection, but his latest performance raises questions about that part of his game.
articles.body:
TreVeyon Henderson's pass-protection struggles are becoming a concern for the New England Patriots , especially considering it was viewed as one of his strengths coming out of college.

The Patriots selected Henderson in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft, with the potential for him to contribute as a runner, receiver and blocker. NFL.com draft analyst Lance Zierlein even described Henderson as potentially the best pass-protecting running back in his draft class.

That assessment makes his latest performance particularly concerning.

Henderson received an 8.6 out of 100 grade in pass protection during Thursday night's 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears, according to a grade shared after the game. He also was the lowest-graded Patriots offensive player.

The rookie finished with three carries for nine yards and caught both of his targets for 14 yards. It was a quiet night overall, but his struggles as a blocker could have a greater impact on his opportunities moving forward.

Pass Protection Could Limit Henderson's Opportunities

Henderson's explosiveness was a major part of his appeal coming out of Ohio State. He led the Patriots in touches, scrimmage yards and touchdowns during his rookie season , establishing himself as a player capable of making an impact in multiple ways.

However, running backs must offer more than big-play potential to earn consistent playing time. Their ability to recognize pressure and protect the quarterback is especially important on passing downs.

Henderson's latest grade raises questions about how reliably he can handle that responsibility. If the Patriots cannot trust him to hold up in pass protection, it could become more difficult to keep him on the field when defenses expect Drake Maye to throw.

That is a difficult situation for New England to navigate with a young player who has already demonstrated his ability to create explosive plays.

Rhamondre Stevenson Has Taken Over the Backfield

Henderson's struggles come as Rhamondre Stevenson continues to handle the majority of the Patriots' backfield work.

Stevenson played 69% of the offensive snaps against Chicago, while Henderson played 24%. Henderson also had his lowest rushing total of the season, finishing with nine yards on three attempts.

The rookie reportedly suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 5 and has continued playing through the injury. That could be affecting his performance, though the extent of any impact remains unclear.

New England still has reason to find ways to use Henderson's speed and playmaking ability. But improving in pass protection would give the second-year running back a better chance to contribute in more situations.

For a player whose pre-draft evaluation highlighted his blocking as a potential strength, turning that part of his game into a reliable asset could be key to earning more opportunities in the Patriots' offense.

articles.title: What happened to Los Angeles Rams’ ‘Super Team’ ahead of Week 7 Las Vegas Raiders matchup?
articles.summary: 5 questions with Turf Show Times
articles.body:
Heading into the season, who would have thought that the Week 7 matchup between the Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams would be a "loser goes home" type of game when it comes to the playoffs? Not many, that's for sure. But here we are.

The 3-3 Raiders need to end a three-game losing streak and beat a quality opponent to be legitimate postseason contenders, while the 2-4 Rams desperately need a win to keep pace in the NFC Wild Card race. To preview the game for Raider Nation, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Turf Show Times, and Kenny Arthur was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Rams.

Q: Sorry, but I have to start with the elephant in the room. The Rams won the offseason and were billed as the heavy Super Bowl favorites heading into the campaign. Sitting at 2-4, how did the "Super Team" fall apart?

A: For the record, I never thought the Rams were a super team, or even the best team in the NFC West. They spent the offseason doing what the Rams always do, which is chasing big names and brushing aside actual weaknesses. To be fair, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson addressed a need at cornerback, and McDuffie was a much better use of a late first-round pick than anyone in the draft would have been. So kudos to L.A. for that, although Watson was an overpay. Even so, he was an overpay to replace one of the worst starters on the team.

None of the other moves were that smart, and the non-moves were terrible miscalculations.

Number one, the Rams had the worst special teams in the NFL last year, and it's been a running theme for L.A. to have bad special teams for at least the last five years. Did they upgrade kicker Harrison Mevis? No. (Mevis was cut last week.) Did they hire a better special teams coordinator? No, they hired Bubba Ventrone, who was fired by the Broncos last year. Did they replace returner Xavier Smith, who fumbled the NFC Championship game away? No, they kept him. (Smith was released last month after the season started).

So number one, the Rams had the 32nd-ranked special teams, and I would've predicted no change there. It's extremely difficult to win the Super Bowl with the worst special teams in football, as the Rams found out last year. So no, I didn't have a lot of respect for their disrespect of special teams .

Number two, instead of using resources to upgrade obvious needs like a linebacker or a receiver (injuries to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are NO surprise) or a safety or a defensive tackle, the Rams trade for Myles Garrett (???) and use a first-round pick on QB Ty Simpson (???). Are you pushing all-in or planning for the future?

Garrett is a Hall of Famer, but he didn't address a weakness, especially by trading away Jared Verse for him. Simpson felt like a reach — I understand the urge to draft a QB when your starter is 38 — but this is less about him. It's more than the Rams always treat rookies like they couldn't possibly help. That's not true. Every year the Super Bowl teams have several key rookies. The Rams used their second-round pick on TE Max Klare, who is fifth string and has one snap this year.

So that's what I'd say about the "super team". The Rams made headlines (like paying Aaron Donald $20-$30 million for one season and he's having zero impact) but they ignored weaknesses. So yes, being 2-4 surprises me, but being far more beatable than they were predicted to be does not.

Q: Matthew Stafford hasn't looked anything like the guy who was last season's MVP, from an outside perspective at least. What's been the difference between this year's version of Stafford and last year's? Are the injuries starting to catch up to him?

A: From 2022-2024, Stafford had a TD rate of 4% and an INT rate of 2%. That's an average of 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions per season and 7.3 Y/A, right? That's three seasons; it's a much larger sample size than one season. That's who he is. That's your basic Matthew Stafford.

Then last season the Rams acquired Davante Adams, and he threw 46 touchdowns. Stafford's TD rate went up to 7.7% and his Y/A went up to 8.8. He had a top-3 WR in Nacua helping him take chunks out of the field on the drive, and then at the goal line Sean McVay would call a pass for Adams. In 2025, Adams caught 11 goal-line touchdowns. McVay turned Stafford into a goal-line back, except with his arm. I say this all to say that Stafford won MVP because McVay changed the goal-line offense into one that favored passes instead of runs, which is what helped Stafford barely beat Drake Maye at the finish line.

Now we've seen a normal Matthew Stafford season again. I think he struggled against the 49ers in Australia in Week 1, and then against the Eagles he wasn't that good, and the goal-line touchdowns went to Kyren Williams. Otherwise, I actually think not much has changed. He's Stafford. He's good. He's not elite. You'd rather have him than most quarterbacks. Puka missed two games; now Adams is out for 6-10 weeks. I think the Rams should have — as I said before — added another receiver in the offseason. Now they're out of money.

Q: A ruptured hamstring robbed us of the Davante Adams revenge game this weekend. So, who is expected to step up and fill the void as Los Angeles' No. 2 pass-catcher behind Puka Nacua?

A: Nobody will step up. Konata Mumpfield might get the reps, but he's not that good. Jordan Whittington isn't that good. Tyler Higbee might get the second-most targets, but he's not that good. Tutu Atwell isn't good. I might think it's tight end Colby Parkinson, but he's having an awful season. The Rams screwed up; they should have used their first-round pick to acquire a receiver somehow.

Q: I'm going to cheat here and ask two defensive line questions. One, how has Aaron Donald looked since coming out of retirement? Two, besides Donald, with Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner and Poona Ford injured and out for Sunday, who is left on the Rams' defensive line?

A: Aaron Donald hasn't looked good. Unfortunately for the Rams, he's still been the best defensive lineman on the roster. The only other guy who might have that distinction is Turner, and he's on IR. Ford could only stop the run; he's arguably the worst pass-rushing defensive tackle in the league. Braden Fiske has regressed badly since his rookie season.

Dare I say that Ashton Jeanty is going to look like a top-10 pick on Sunday? This might be the worst defensive line in football.

You'll see guys named Tyler Davis and Ty Hamilton. That's about all I can say about them. Larrell Murchison too.

Q: Los Angeles' defense is interesting on paper because despite ranking third in yards allowed , the unit is 17th in points surrendered heading into Week 7. What's led to that anomaly? If you were Klint Kubiak, how would you attack the Rams' defense?

A: Ask yourself when the Rams' defensive stats improved. Against Jameis Winston in Week 2 (when he replaced Jaxson Dart) and against Jalen Hurts in Week 4. And against Bo Nix. Last week it was Jacoby Brissett. Josh Allen and James Cook had no problems. Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey had no problems. If the team has talent at QB and RB/OL, I wouldn't think twice about having a banner day against L.A.

Given how well Klint Kubiak seems to have done with Kirk Cousins this season (you know better than I do if that's true), I expect an ugly day for the Rams defense. McDuffie was out last week; I'm not sure if he'll be back this week. The Rams' best players are McDuffie and Garrett, and both could be out. Without those two, the defense is downright bad. Attack them however you want.

I'll be called a "hater" by Rams fans, and "not a Rams fan" because of these answers. This is merely what I've observed from a 2-4 season with wins over the Giants and Eagles, and just losing to the Cardinals. In the same way that the Chargers are 0-6, should we say that the Chargers "aren't that bad" because they looked better on paper? Or should we call a spade a spade? This is a very interesting matchup with another team that badly needs to stop the bleeding. I don't know who will win, but given how banged up L.A. is this week, it could definitely be the Raiders.

articles.title: 49ers Given Clear Option to Trade QB Mac Jones Before Deadline
articles.summary: Over the last couple of years, the San Francisco 49ers have been connected to quite a few rumors surrounding quarterback Mac Jones. Last season, Jones steppe...
articles.body:
Over the last couple of years, the San Francisco 49ers have been connected to quite a few rumors surrounding quarterback Mac Jones.

Last season, Jones stepped in for Brock Purdy when the starter went down with injury early in the year. Jones performed admirably, proving that he was still capable of being a starting NFL quarterback.

In 11 games played in 2025, the 28-year-old quarterback completed 69.6 percent of his pass attempts for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He has yet to throw a pass this season. That has led to more rumors before the upcoming November 10 trade deadline.

Jones could simply remain with the 49ers and give the team excellent backup quarterback depth. If something were to happen to Purdy, San Francisco would be able to continue performing at a high level offensively.

Should John Lynch and the 49ers' front office decide to open up to the idea of trading Jones, a few different teams would likely have interest. With that being said, one team in particular has been connected to a possible trade for Jones.

49ers Handed Clear-Cut Trade Destination for QB Mac Jones

The Athletic has released a big board of 50 potential trade candidates before the 2026 deadline. When it came to Jones, they only suggested on landing spot.

That landing spot was none other than the Philadelphia Eagles, who recently ruled Jalen Hurts out for the rest of the season due to blood clot issues.

"Jones is one of the best backup quarterbacks in the league. He should, at some point, get another chance to start. That will most likely come in 2027, as Jones is in the final year of a two-year deal he signed with the 49ers," they wrote.

"But could a team in need of a quarterback — like the Eagles, if they don't take the retool avenue — convince the 49ers to make a deal with an over-the-top offer? It's unlikely. But again, we're trying to have fun here. The 49ers are contenders after a 6-0 start, and keeping some insurance behind MVP frontrunner Brock Purdy makes more sense."

After being selected with the No. 15 overall pick by the New England Patriots in the 2021 NFL Draft, Jones struggled to find consistency. He has played in 64 total games, throwing for 12,741 yards, 67 touchdowns, and 50 interceptions.

More than likely, the 49ers will simply hold onto Jones through the deadline. But, the Eagles are a team worth monitoring if Lynch decides to consider a move.

articles.title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin’s status for Lions bout revealed in latest injury update
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions after he suffered a shin injury during practice on Th...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions after he suffered a shin injury during practice on Thursday. Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Friday that the veteran defensive captain has been ruled out .

Franklin's absence creates another challenge for Green Bay's defense, which has already lost starting linebacker Edgerrin Cooper for the season because of an Achilles tendon tear. Cooper suffered the injury in Week 4, leaving the Packers without both of their Week 1 starting linebackers for the trip to Detroit.

LaFleur indicated that Franklin is not expected to require injured reserve, which would force him to miss at least four games. However, the team is still assessing the severity of his injury.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The 30-year-old has been a key contributor through six games, leading the Packers with 48 tackles and ranking second on the team with 15 stops, according to Pro Football Focus. He has also played 414 defensive snaps this season.

With Franklin unavailable, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper are expected to take on larger responsibilities. McDuffie has started in Cooper's place over the past two weeks, while Hopper, a 2024 third-round draft pick, could receive an opportunity to play a more regular defensive role. Nick Niemann and veteran special-teamer Kristian Welch are also options for the linebacker rotation.

Green Bay will face a big test against the Lions' running game, led by running back Jahmyr Gibbs. He has recorded 504 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns, ranking fifth in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for second in rushing scores. He has also produced 27 receptions for 243 yards and two receiving touchdowns.

Detroit's offense is averaging 32.8 points per game, tied with the Buffalo Bills for the league lead. The Lions have also exploited McDuffie in the past as quarterback Jared Goff completed all nine passes thrown toward the linebacker in their 2024 meeting, producing 68 yards and a touchdown in the team's 34-31 win .

The timing of his latest injury could hardly be worse for Franklin, as the Packers are scheduled to play on Thursday Night Football in Week 8, potentially extending his absence to a second game. It would be a rare setback for the defender, who had missed only one game throughout his NFL career before the latest setback.

articles.title: The Rams were Super Bowl favorites. Now they're fighting a 30-year curse
articles.summary: Over the past 30 years, the preseason Super Bowl favorite entered the season with +500 or better odds 20 times. None have gone on to win the title.
articles.body:
It happens every year. A team lights the NFL world on fire with Super Bowl hope and expectation in the preseason, only to flop and fall short of a Lombardi once the season begins. And by "it happens every year," we literally mean it happens every year .

The Los Angeles Rams entered the 2026 season as +500 — that is, 5-1 — Super Bowl favorites. You know what's happened since — the Rams are currently 2-4, victims of injury and curiously bad performances. A Super Bowl is still very much in play, but if Los Angeles ends up failing to win it all, they'll join an illustrious lineage.

As Yahoo Sports senior betting analyst Ben Fawkes notes, not one of the teams in the past 30 years that began the season with +500 or better odds to win the Super Bowl actually ended up winning. Twenty teams began the year with those kinds of favorable conditions, and all twenty failed to close the deal. Some failed early, some only fell short in the final seconds of the Super Bowl.

For instance, everyone knew the 2007 Patriots were absolutely loaded, which is why they went off at +250 and won every game right up until they faced the Giants in the Super Bowl. The 2014 Seahawks (+450) were coming off a Super Bowl victory and were poised to grab another, right up until the Patriots' Malcolm Butler intervened. Most recently, the 2024 Chiefs (+500) bulldozed their way through the regular season with a 15-2 record, and cruised right up until they ran out of gas against the Eagles in the Super Bowl.

There are two factors at play here. First is the inherent unpredictability of football. A team getting +500 odds before the season even begins only actually has an implied probability of 16.67 percent of winning the Super Bowl. And as any Patriots fan who remembers Manning-to-Tyree or the Philly Special can tell you, there's no such thing as certain Super Bowl victory before kickoff.

"It's one of the things that bettors and the fans love about the NFL," Fawkes says. "If it was that easy, then everyone would just bet on the favorite and collect their winnings at +500, +400, +300. And a lot of people would be living on small, nice islands."

The second factor is the alchemy in how preseason odds are calculated. Sportsbooks, analysts, columnists and fans alike all begin with a baseline of expectation based on prior-year results. Teams that were good last year, assuming no major personnel losses, will likely be good again this year. It's then that group psychology takes over; when bettors begin flocking to one team over all others, sportsbooks will adjust the line accordingly to protect themselves.

"The true chances [of winning] aren't necessarily the odds that are being offered," Fawkes says. "Especially with a team with a lot of public groundswell and support like the Rams, oddsmakers are going to bump those up even more."

Looking over that list of preseason Super Bowl favorites that fell short, you can spot this obvious trend: bettors flocking to familiar teams, whether it's Patrick Mahomes' Chiefs, Tom Brady's Patriots or the mid-2010s Legion of Boom Seahawks. Familiarity draws money.

Sportsbooks try to limit their exposure to significant losses by lowering the odds of notable or often-bet teams; it's why LeBron James' 76ers have low odds now, and why Tiger Woods had low odds every time he entered a tournament even when he was hardly able to walk the course.

The teams that come out of nowhere — the Kurt Warner-led Rams of 1999, for instance, or the Nick Foles-led Eagles back in 2017 — are the ones that pay off, simply because they're so unexpected. (According to BetMGM, this year's largest liabilities for sportsbooks are the Raiders, Steelers and Browns, should any of them manage an improbable Super Bowl win.)

As always, it's worth remembering that casinos don't get built because they lose money:

The Rams specifically ended up in this situation because of a confluence of factors; the team may well have been the best in the league last year, falling just four points short of a Super Bowl appearance. The addition of Myles Garrett only bolstered their chances, in theory, leading bettors to flock to the Rams.

On the day before the 2026 season opened, according to BetMGM, Rams Super Bowl futures led the NFL in both ticket percentage (9.5 percent) and handle (money wagered, 15.7 percent). That potential liability had moved the line from its opening at +900 to +500. Today, that line stands at +1200, although the Rams still have the second-highest ticket and handle percentages, behind Buffalo. (Your current leader: San Francisco at +550.)

The reasons for the Rams' sudden downfall include injuries and a corresponding lack of depth, concerns that look obvious in retrospect but minimal in the moment. There's still plenty of time for Los Angeles to get itself back on the right track and validate the faith of those many preseason bettors, but if the Rams can't pull it off, they'll join some notable company.

articles.title: Analyst’s source has ‘known Arch Manning a long time’ and makes transfer portal prediction for 2027
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns entered the season with national title expectations, but consecutive losses to the Oklahoma Sooners and Florida Gators have the program’s...
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns entered the season with national title expectations, but consecutive losses to the Oklahoma Sooners and Florida Gators have the program's College Football Playoff chances on thin ice, and quarterback Arch Manning has been at the center of the struggles.

In a column for Bleacher Report, Adam Kramer argued that it might be time for Manning and Texas to part ways.

"This would be best for Manning; it would also make sense for Texas," Kramer wrote. "This once-promising football marriage has lost its luster. And there's no salvaging it now," Kramer wrote.

Kramer isn't alone, either. NFL draft analyst Todd McShay has also floated the possibility of Arch returning to college and transferring rather than entering the transfer portal.

"Arch Manning — Return. Explore a transfer? — There's still time to turn this season around. I'm more bullish on his NFL future than the social media doom suggests, but another college season currently looks like his best path," McShay posted on X.

It would appear that where there's smoke, there's fire. On a recent episode of the Bill Simmons Podcast, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero revealed what someone who has known Manning for a long time believes next year has in store for the young quarterback.

"I texted one person who's known Arch (Manning) a long time earlier tonight, and I said, 'Where do you see Arch in 2027?' And his response was Ole Miss," Pelissero said.

For now, Manning is still the Longhorns quarterback, and his head coach, Steve Sarkisian, has made it clear what he and the program need from the offense's leader.

"I think that somebody texted me today that we lost the 'Aw Shucks' kid and we created something else. I don't know if we lost him," Sarkisian said. "We created this. We did. All of us. Y'all included. Me. The whole thing, right. Everybody on ESPN, we've created this. And so we'll see what comes out of it.

"But he's edgy right now. And honestly, I appreciate that about him. At some point, he's gotta fight back," Sarkisian said. "And the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates and enjoy playing football with his teammates. And so I'm looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night."

Ironically, Texas will face Ole Miss in primetime on Saturday night.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Reveals Severity of Ankle Injury, Latest on QB's Status for Ravens vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson says he is "heading in the right direction" and could play in Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after returning to practice earlier this week as he recovers from a high ankle sprain.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson says he is "heading in the right direction" and could play in Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after returning to practice earlier this week as he recovers from a high ankle sprain.

"I can't call it right now. Still got a grace period. We'll see, man. Hopefully," Jackson said Friday. "But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now."

Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson had gone through "a good couple of days" since rejoining practice in a limited capacity this week for the first time since Week 4.

"It's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective... he feels like he can be," Minter said (h/t ESPN's Jamison Hensley).

After avoiding injuries through the first three games of the season, Jackson exited the Ravens' Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans due to an ankle injury.

The ankle injury forced Jackson to miss the last two games, and Baltimore has gone 1-1 during that stretch. He reportedly had a chance to play in the Ravens' Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, but ultimately wasn't ready to return as Baltimore lost 13-10.

In four games, Jackson has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, adding 144 yards and a score on the ground. The Ravens are sitting at 4-2 on the season heading into this week's matchup against the Bengals.

Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson in his absence and has collected 429 passing yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions.

Injuries have unfortunately been the story for Jackson over the last two seasons. He missed four games last year and finished the 2025 campaign with 2,549 passing yards, 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions, while rushing for 349 yards and two touchdowns.

The Ravens finished the season 8-9 and missed the playoffs, and they're hoping to avoid a repeat of the 2025 campaign.

articles.title: Discipline of guarding 24 seconds: Scheierman on how Boston Celtics beat Knicks
articles.summary: "I think it comes down to our discipline of staying consistent throughout the possession," he added.
articles.body:
It might only be the start of the third season of Baylor Scheierman's NBA career since being picked up by the Boston Celtics with the 30th overall selection of the 2024 NBA Draft, but he has plenty of experience on how to play the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks with a total of 8 regular season tilts with the Knicks plus a 6-game postseason series vs. New York to his name already.

And the Nebraska native had some words to that effect ahead of what will be his ninth collision with the Knicks in the regular season after a Celtics practice on Friday (Oct. 23) morning. "It comes down to the discipline of guarding for 24 seconds," he explained via CLNS Media.

"They like to push it, and then if it's not there, it really works the box," Scheierman continued. "So I think it comes down to our discipline of staying consistent throughout the possession, and then finishing possessions with rebounds."

New York's two biggest stars, Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, stood out as particular challenges to the Creighton alum. "One, they're tough shot makers," he said.

"And then two, they play well off of each other and you have to be disciplined because they're looking for any sort of angle they can get on you. Especially playing downhill playing off two feet shot fakes stuff like that so it's just a lot of discipline."

Boston will need all it can find to avoid starting their season in a 0-2 deficit. But if the Celtics clean up the late-game issues that doomed them on Opening Night vs. the Detroit Pistons , they just might have a shot.
