articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 7 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Jameson Williams or Jaylen Waddle?
articles.summary: An analysis of statistics, matchups, & all fantasy football factors to determine which of Jameson Williams or Jaylen Waddle is the better Week 7 wide receive...
articles.body:
If you own Jameson Williams or Jaylen Waddle in fantasy football, then I understand the frustration. They are WR39 and WR41, respectively. With top-20 hopes before the season started, the results haven't been pleasant. The good news is that the NFL is a week-to-week environment. A player can turn his season around in a blink. We hope to see that happen in Week 7. As for which wideout is the better play? I debate the following.

Williams has five games played on his 2026 resume. He averages 5.8 targets, 3.6 receptions, 55.2 yards, and 0.4 touchdowns per game. Williams averages 1.50 Yards per Route Run (NFL average: roughly 1.75), a 14.7% target share, 32% of air yards, and about a 90% snap rate.

In such a start-sit debate, I emphasize usage over projected output. As volatile as any NFL game might be, a high projection could easily miss. A team may not get the time of possession they expected; they may enter an unexpected game script, and that possession expectation can lead to a projection miss.

Thus, I favor projected offense volume as it plays safer in such a start-sit debate.

Williams isn't just playing 90% of the snaps; when he's on the field, he runs routes 97% of the time. In any passing situation, he goes out for a catch, not to block. He runs 11 more routes per game than the Lions' next wide receiver, Isaac Teslaa. He runs almost the exact same amount as Amon-Ra St. Brown and 4.0 more routes per game than Sam LaPorta.

Despite a weak target share, Williams has commendable volume. He should begin to see an uptick in fantasy production, as a 14.7% target share is unlikely to hold up given his playing time.

Williams is competing against the Green Bay Packers. Their defense ranks 13th-best in Yards per Target Allowed to outside wide receivers like Williams. His slot rate is just 24%.

The Packers play zone coverage at the 5th-highest rate in the NFL (75%). That bodes well for Williams, who averages 1.93 PPR Fantasy Points per Target against zone and 1.20 against man coverage.

Waddle has played six games in 2026. He averages 6.3 targets, 3.7 receptions, 38.0 yards, and 0.17 touchdowns per game. Waddle averages 1.49 Yards per Route Run on a 19.0% target share, 38.0% of air yards, and a 79% snap share.

On Waddle's passing snaps, he runs a route 91% of the time. He ranks second on the Broncos in routes run per game, 2.9 fewer than Courtland Sutton. Waddle runs nearly double the routes, twice as many as any other wide receiver on the team.

The season isn't much a fault of Waddle's; it's the Broncos' and Bo Nix's. Waddle has a career yards-per-reception of 13.4, and just 10.4 in 2026 because of Nix's checkdown-heavy philosophy this season. Added to the lower total, Waddle still has a 59% catch rate.

Waddle will compete against the Arizona Cardinals this weekend. They rank 2nd-worst in Yards per Target Allowed to Wide Receivers (9.9), only behind the Jacksonville Jaguars. Waddle plays a mix of routes from the slot and outside.

The good news for Waddle is that the Cardinals play the 2nd-highest rate of man coverage, 45%. Waddle averages 0.86 more Yards per route run (2.31) versus man coverage. However, he is good against either coverage for the most part.

Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Jameson Williams or Jaylen Waddle?

Waddle is ultimately the sharper play of the two. Though Williams has a slightly higher snap rate, he has had less pass volume and a smaller share to date. Waddle has the better coverage matchup and has better per-route statistics. Neither player has more than three red zone targets this season, so err on the side of volume rather than banking on touchdown(s).

In Week 7, Waddle is a capable, must-start WR2 with lower-end upside. Williams is also worth starting, given his snap share, but he's more of a WR3/Flex play.

articles.title: Bears TE Cole Kmet out for the season after suffering knee injury vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Kmet was injured late in the fourth quarter of the Bears' win over the Patriots.
articles.body:
The right knee injury suffered by tight end Cole Kmet during the Chicago Bears' Thursday night win over the New England Patriots has ended his season.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Kmet will go on injured reserve after tests revealed the severity of the injury.

"He's Chicago," Johnson said. "He's been here his whole life. He's a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks."

Kmet was carted off late in the fourth quarter after making an 8-yard catch. As he ran toward the first-down marker, he was hit by Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and linebacker Robert Spillane and immediately began clutching his knee.

After getting assisted to his feet by athletic trainers, Kmet was carted off as he could not put weight on his right leg. He gave a thumbs-up to the Soldier Field crowd as he left the field. The team ruled him out for the rest of the game a short while later.

"I don't think it looked very good," Johnson said afterward.

The 27-year-old Kmet is in his seventh season with the Bears. Through seven games this season he has 10 receptions for 87 yards and a touchdown. Against the Patriots, he made three catches for 28 yards before exiting.

articles.title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) 'headed in the right direction,' could be game-time decision vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Jackson has been out with a high ankle sprain since Week 4.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson took part in practice for the third straight day on Friday, an encouraging sign for the Baltimore Ravens quarterback's chances of playing against the Cincinnati Bengals.

But while it was good to see Jackson in practice again after missing two games due to a high ankle sprain suffered in Week 4, no one is ready to declare him 100% back for Sunday.

"He's been able to get some work in these past couple of days," head coach Jesse Minter said . "Between Lamar and our staff, it's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective it could be. He's had a good couple of days, but we'll see how it goes over the next 48 hours."

Minter added he wasn't sure how Jackson would be listed on the team's Friday injury report and that a final decision on his status could come close to game time.

Jackson missed two weeks of practice following the injury, but the work he's done off the field has him in a place for a possible return this weekend.

"Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson said about his status for Week 7. "We'll see, hopefully."

Jackson said the biggest factor in whether he plays this week is not any swelling, but how much of the pain he can deal with.

"I feel like the swelling went down a lot," Jackson said. "It's just the pain tolerance. Just trying to move how I move. If I can't do that, I can't help my team."

Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson since the injury. He entered the game against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 and helped Baltimore to a win. He has since started each of the past two weeks — a win over the Atlanta Falcons and a defeat to the Cleveland Browns. In those two starts he's thrown for 336 yards with three touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 68% pass completion percentage.

"It's just like every week," Huntley said of potentially getting a third straight start. "Just prepare to play and then once we get to Sunday we'll see."

articles.title: Baker Mayfield set to start for Bucs' Week 7 game vs. Panthers; WR Emeka Egbuka ruled out with concussion
articles.summary: Mayfield practiced in full all week and is poised to return to game action following a three-game absence that stemmed from him dislocating the thumb on his...
articles.body:
Baker Mayfield is set to make his return Sunday in Carolina, according to Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles, who told reporters Friday that his two-time Pro Bowl quarterback looks "ready to go" for the road game versus the Panthers.

Although Mayfield is technically listed as "questionable" on the Bucs' injury report , he was a full participant in practice all week .

His expected return will mark his first game since Sept. 27. Back then, during a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, Mayfield dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand . Mayfield's three-week recovery timeline was reportedly the best-case scenario.

Even though Mayfield is re-entering the lineup, he won't have one of his top wideouts to throw to, as Tampa Bay ruled out Emeka Egbuka on Friday. Egbuka's been in concussion protocol this week.

Egbuka didn't leave last week's overtime defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers with the injury. It wasn't until he was back in facility this week that his symptoms surfaced, leading to him being placed in the protocol, as reported by ESPN's Jenna Laine .

Bowles said Friday, via Laine , that the Bucs couldn't figure out which play Egbuka suffered the concussion. Notably, Egbuka absorbed a fourth-quarter blow from Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen, whose shoulder collided with Egbuka's helmet on an incomplete pass.

But Bowles said Friday that "there were several plays that it could have happened or not happened on."

Egbuka, who's also dealing with a foot issue, currently leads the 1-5 Buccaneers with 28 receptions and 240 receiving yards. The second-year pro also has a team-high two touchdown grabs.

In addition to missing Egbuka, Tampa Bay will be down right tackle Luke Goedeke. He'll be sidelined with a calf injury that he picked up last week.

Despite those absences, Mayfield will have to deliver a much-needed win against the NFC South rival Panthers.

In Mayfield's place, the Bucs turned to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. He went 1-2 in his three starts, highlighted by a "Thursday Night Football" win over the Dallas Cowboys.

But the Kansas product has posted a meager 3:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio over four appearances, with two of those picks coming last week against the Steelers. Daniels threw a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions, and Tampa Bay blew a 13-point lead in the final frame .
